items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I mean like Joe Helblock, next door at the Onyx Club, was very liberally minded.

ctx.x: Even on 52nd Street, or especially on 52nd Street, or how --

Well, now, it depended on the bosses. I mean, you'd get right down to it. I mean like Joe Helblock, next door at the Onyx Club, was very liberally minded. There wasn't any problem there. Whereas, at the Famous Door, where both of these incidents took place, the management there wasn't, while they employed black orchestras, they apparently didn't want anybody to mix up. I did not have a mixed band in there. And of course that was -- we're going way ahead of it. We're getting up -- but although -- I think it had to…
But on 52nd Street, at the Famous Door, you weren't allowed to? You just didn't happen to have or you were not allowed to have a mixed band?
